text: Bright Memory is a gorgeous, fast-paced action sampler that punches way above its single-dev weight class. The juggling mechanics and grappling-hook combat are addictively fun, though the experience is over in the blink of an eye. If you find it on a deep sale, it's a stellar forty-five minutes of pure eye candy and stylish violence.
I was not expecting the story that this game provided when I first played it. I was absolutely swept off my feet, what a unique experience and it's like 3 games in one without saying any more!

One of the best games I've played in my whole life.

Stellar writing, satisfying gameplay, incredible characters - that you actually care about. 
Johnny Silverhand, specifically, is unforgettable - Keanu did an amazing job as him. 
The whole experience is perfected by an masterpiece of a soundtrack. The menu music, and the Phantom Liberty credits hits so damn hard. 
Story is extremely engaging, although, my only complain is the dissonance between the story's urgency, and the actual gameplay - you are dying, and yet you are wasting precious time doing 1000 gigs, side-quests, and side activities - BECAUSE THEY ARE JUST AS GOOD AS THE MAIN STORY - but that's just how videogame works lol. I'm serious though, the side stuff in this game is REALLY good.

Overall, this game is a masterpiece, and I will never stop glazing it - EVERYONE should try it at least once in their lives.

Just finished, it's fun. Game is gorgeous, probably spent a good 15 minutes just getting caught up in the visuals and staring off into the skyboxes. Not too difficult, and a little short, but it has the bones of a fantastic game given some fleshing out. The skill tree is pretty neat though I wish you could branch a little in different directions. There are 4 nodes that take your progression in different directions, but you can only select one of those 4 nodes. If you want any of the benefits of that side of the circle after that you have to wrap around in your skill tree, which can make some basic upgrades like larger health pools or greater melee damage inaccessible if you go the wrong direction to start. Maybe some kind of rarer drop that lets you take another of the 4 primary nodes would be nice. Anyhow, cool game, definitely recommend.

it's been about 3 years since i first played and i still think about this game all the time. it's such a beautiful reflection on how citizens of once tight-knit, labor-driven towns cope with the erosion of their community via late-stage capitalism. i felt the struggle for survival. the melancholy. the grief. the disaffection. the anxiety. and the moments of levity that made it all, somehow, worth trekking on. as far as point and click adventures go, this is as good as it gets. and i'll be waiting with bated breath for whatever geography of robots puts out next.

Great game. I wish there was an option to enable music after defeating the boss in each area. I defeated the boss as soon as I collected 6 lightstones to get a more relaxed open world puzzle solving experience, but the music is turned off by the developer, who's trying to make a point. 

Also, mountain tundra's red cast (after defeating boss) physically burned my eyes. It was purely by chance that I realized I could turn it off. Why the red cast to begin with? It ruined the scenery.

But other than those two issues, great game. Beautiful world building. Immersive atmosphere. Puzzles get too easy after a point but still great. I enjoyed Abzu and this game did not disappoint. Thank you for the hard work.

Besides the fact this game has no one playing it. My friend and I bought the game. We had a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blast. The bots do try to murder you if they are the killer. Yeah, a bit, there is a delay in when the game announces someone dies. A mic bug that's solved by leaving the lobby and coming back. Those are my biggest issues. However, I love the look of it cause it's like those old PS2 games honestly. I've seen worse graphics. This game is fun and we bought it on a sale. I hope it comes out this year too, cause I would like to play it with my friends.
